taxonomy.subtopic: Loss of nigrostriatal dopamine and increased globus pallidus internus output

questions.stem_html: A 71-year-old man has bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, a resting tremor, and a shuffling gait. The accompanying basal-ganglia schematic marks degeneration of substantia nigra pars compacta neurons. Which downstream change is most directly responsible for his reduced initiation of movement?

options.text_html: Increased activation of direct-pathway striatal neurons through D1 receptors
Increased inhibitory output from the globus pallidus internus to the thalamus
Decreased excitatory output from the subthalamic nucleus to the globus pallidus internus
Increased inhibition of the indirect-pathway striatal neurons through D2 receptors
Decreased inhibitory output from the substantia nigra pars reticulata to motor thalamus

questions.explanation_html: Nigrostriatal dopamine normally promotes movement by stimulating D1 direct-pathway neurons and inhibiting D2 indirect-pathway neurons. Loss of dopamine weakens the direct pathway and strengthens the indirect pathway. The subthalamic nucleus consequently drives the globus pallidus internus more strongly, increasing GABAergic inhibition of motor thalamus and reducing thalamocortical excitation.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: The indirect pathway increases subthalamic nucleus activity in dopamine deficiency, so excitatory drive to the globus pallidus internus rises.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Dopamine normally inhibits D2 indirect-pathway neurons; loss of dopamine removes this inhibition.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Dopamine normally stimulates D1 direct-pathway neurons; their activity falls when nigrostriatal dopamine is lost.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Reduced inhibitory basal-ganglia output would facilitate movement, the opposite of the parkinsonian state.

questions.educational_objective: Loss of substantia nigra pars compacta dopamine reduces direct-pathway activity and increases indirect-pathway activity, raising GPi inhibition of the thalamus and suppressing movement.

media.alt_text: Original basal ganglia circuit showing loss of substantia nigra dopamine, reduced direct-pathway drive, enhanced indirect-pathway influence, and increased globus pallidus internus inhibition of thalamus.
